archetype.name: Breakthrough Season (short of contention)
archetype.definition: Pittsburgh posted its first winning record in the six seasons on the sheet and a positive run differential, but it was never close to the division's top two and missed the postseason.

report.headline: Lineup jumps from 30th to 6th, and Pittsburgh finally finishes above .500

recap.finish: 82-80, third in the NL Central, 7 games behind CHC and 21 behind MIL; missed the postseason
recap.body:
This was a different Pirates team than the one the sheet shows for 2025. That club prevented runs (5th) and could not score (30th, a .655 OPS). The 2026 version flipped that. The offense climbed to 6th in runs per game with a .734 OPS, while run prevention slipped to 19th. Netting out at +0.17 runs per game, 11th in the majors, was enough for 82 wins and a site rank of 13th. The last five seasons on the sheet all ranked 21st or worse.

The season came in three stretches. A 16-12 May put them at 32-28 and looking like a real riser. June through August then went 35-43, and by the end of August they were 67-71. The August slump was an offense problem: 97 runs in 27 games, about 3.6 a game, down from roughly 4.9 in July. Run prevention in August was actually among the best of their year. September's 15-9 finish, including 7-3 over the last ten, lifted them above .500. That month was outscored-adjusted luck, though. They scored 98 and allowed 96, and most of those final ten games were decided by one run.

The lineup's production was concentrated. Brandon Lowe was the engine, with 4.9 WAR, 35 home runs, a 121 wRC+ and +9.9 Def Runs at second base. Oneil Cruz had the best bat on the team (132 wRC+, 30 steals) but played only 97 games. Bryan Reynolds (118 wRC+ over 699 PA) and Nick Gonzales (.303/.367) gave them steady on-base presence. That concentration explains how a 6th-ranked offense still graded C- as a hitting group. A lot of plate appearances went to below-average bats:
- the Ryan O'Hearn/Spencer Horwitz first-base pairing ranked 35th and 36th of 44 at the position
- Jake Mangum posted a 91 wRC+
- Jared Triolo posted a 70 wRC+ in 362 PA at shortstop, where Konnor Griffin was the better option when he played

The pitching grades say B+ for both rotation and bullpen, yet team ERA was only 16th. Some of that gap belongs to the defense. Fielding Runs of -20.7 ranked 23rd, with Gonzales (-7.7) and Griffin (-5.8) the biggest leaks. Paul Skenes (3.82 ERA, 3.33 FIP, 200 K) and Jared Jones (3.72 ERA, 3.22 FIP) both pitched better than their run totals. Braxton Ashcraft gave them a second All-Star starter. The back of the rotation was where runs got through: Bubba Chandler walked 11.9% of batters, and Mitch Keller had a 5.29 ERA before landing on the 60-day IL. In the bullpen, Mason Montgomery was elite, with a 37.8% K rate, 2.36 FIP and 18 saves, ranking 6th of 389 relievers. Gregory Soto shared closing duty.

Over the full year the record undersold the team slightly. A W vs Run Diff of -1.8 says the run differential supported closer to 84 wins. That wouldn't have changed the outcome: second place in the Central went to Chicago at 89-73. What the season establishes is a floor. This roster outscored its opponents across 162 games, which no Pirates team on the sheet had done.

highlights.title: Offense went from last to sixth
highlights.body: The lineup's OPS rose from .655 and 30th in 2025 to .734 and 6th. Runs per game ranked 6th as well. Lowe's 35 homers and Cruz's 132 wRC+ drove most of it, with Reynolds and Gonzales getting on base around them. The production is real but narrow: two or three bats carried a group that graded only C-.

highlights.title: Rotation top three, plus Jones
highlights.body: Skenes, Ashcraft and Jones all posted ERAs under 3.85 and FIPs at 3.50 or better, which earned the rotation its B+. Skenes' 3.33 FIP against a 3.82 ERA suggests the defense behind him cost him runs, not his stuff. This core is the most durable asset the season shows.

highlights.title: Montgomery anchored a B+ bullpen
highlights.body: Montgomery struck out 37.8% of batters with a 2.36 FIP and 18 saves. Soto and Yohan Ramírez added depth behind him. Ramírez's 12.2% walk rate and Lake Bachar's 3.43 ERA against a 4.32 FIP are the soft spots, so expect some regression below the top.

lowlights.title: Defense gave back the pitching gains
lowlights.body: At -20.7 Fielding Runs, 23rd, the gloves help explain why B+ pitching groups produced only a 16th-ranked team ERA and 19th in run prevention. The left side of the infield was the worst of it, with Gonzales at -7.7 and Griffin at -5.8. The 2024 club had a similar -23.8, so this is a recurring weakness, not a one-year blip.

lowlights.title: Thin bats behind the core
lowlights.body: First base produced two hitters ranked 35th and 36th of 44 at the position. Triolo's 70 wRC+ took 362 PA at shortstop. That is why a top-six offense still graded C-. The August collapse to about 3.6 runs a game showed how little cushion there was when the top of the order cooled.

lowlights.title: Back of the rotation leaked
lowlights.body: Chandler's 11.9% walk rate and Keller's 5.29 ERA took up nearly 270 innings combined. Keller ended the year on the 60-day IL, and Jones made only 21 starts. Depth behind the top three is the rotation's open question.

arc.note: They peaked at 32-28 after May and sagged to 67-71 through August as the offense dried up. A 15-9 September built on one-run wins pulled them over .500; streaks never ran longer than five either way.

recap.nextYear:
The carry-over pieces are clear. Lowe, Cruz and Reynolds powered the lineup. Skenes, Ashcraft and Jones give the rotation a sound top three, and Montgomery is a genuine late-inning weapon. The work is in the margins:
- **Lineup depth:** first base and shortstop, where the playing time went to bats graded well below average.
- **Defense:** -20.7 Fielding Runs that hid what the pitching was doing.
- **Rotation depth:** the fourth and fifth starters.

On luck, the full-season W vs Run Diff of -1.8 means 82 wins slightly understated a team that played to about 84. The 15-9 September on a +2 run margin overstated how strong the finish was, so don't read the closing kick as a new level. A +0.17 differential is a fringe-contender baseline, not a playoff one. Closing the seven-game gap to second place depends more on fixing the bottom of the roster than on the stars repeating.

confidence.note: Full 162-game season; the patterns line up with the group grades and the history.
